<reason>PRO set the decisive burden - how a ban leaves the woman who still signs better off - and CON never met it. PRO showed bans export demand to unprotected markets while domestic regulation retains most cases with counsel, escrow, and void body-control clauses. CON's advertise-the-market and money-enforces-void-clauses points were eloquent but relied on asserted deterrence, and conceded the Ukrainian woman is not directly protected. Execution cost to PRO for two clipped endings does not outweigh that comparative edge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's poverty-consent turn plus unpaid-surrogacy pressure: if poverty voids consent all poor women's work is indicted, void clauses make buyer expectation give, and identical risks in England/Canada force CON to admit the target is the paycheck, not hemorrhage or grief.</best_rebuttal>
